case_name: Rubabbuddin Sheikh v State Of Gujarat And Ors
facts: Acting on a letter written by the writ petitioner, Rubabbuddin Sheikh, to the Chief Justice of India about the killing of his brother, Sohrabuddin Sheikh in a fake encounter and disappearance of his sister-in-law Kausarbi at the hands of the Anti Terrorist Squad (ATS) Gujarat Police and Rajasthan Special Task Force (RSTF), the Registry of this Court forwarded the letter to the Director General of Police, Gujarat to take action.
A case was registered as Enquiry No. 66 of 2006.

The writ petitioner seeks a direction for investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (in short the 'CBI') into the alleged abduction and fake encounter of the brother of the writ petitioner Sohrabuddin by the Gujarat Police Authorities.

The writ petitioner also seeks the registration of an offence and investigation by the CBI into the alleged encounter of one Tulsiram, a close associate of Sohrabuddin, who was allegedly used to locate and abduct Sohrabuddin and his wife Kausarbi, and was thus a material witness against the Police personnel.
The writ petitioner further seeks a writ of habeas corpus to produce Kausarbi, the sister-in-law of the writ petitioner.
issues: Whether the CBI should take over the investigation from the State Investigating Agency?
Whether the State of Gujarat has conducted a fair and impartial investigation into the alleged fake encounter and disappearance of Kausarbi?
petitioner_arguments: The writ petitioner argues that the CBI should take over the investigation to ensure a thorough and impartial inquiry.
The writ petitioner also argues that the State of Gujarat has not conducted a fair and impartial investigation into the alleged fake encounter and disappearance of Kausarbi.
respondent_arguments: The respondent State of Gujarat argues that it has conducted a fair and impartial investigation into the alleged fake encounter and disappearance of Kausarbi.

The respondent State of Gujarat also argues that the CBI should not take over the investigation, as it would be difficult for the Investigating Agency of the State of Gujarat to make proper and thorough enquiry and submit a report to this Court.
court_reasoning: This Court held the view that a prima facie case was made out for issuance of a Rule Nisi calling upon the Union of India and the State of Gujarat to show cause why the order prayed for should not be granted and also as to why a writ of Habeas Corpus should not be issued to produce Kausarbi in Court.
This Court restrained itself from issuing a formal writ and directed the State of Gujarat to submit the final status report within two weeks from that date.
holding: The Court ordered that some more time may be granted to the State of Gujarat before any further action was taken in the matter.

The Court also directed the State of Gujarat to submit a report on the investigation conducted by them and to permit Ms. Johri and Mr. Rajneesh Rai to make the investigation jointly and submit a report to this Court.
